correctness.rationale: The exact perimeter of a central section is four explicit elliptical arcs plus two cap chords. For t>h, after x=sin φ the Euclidean integral triangle inequality gives P/(4R)≥sqrt(h²+α²)+cos α. Its derivative has sign αcotα−h, with αcotα strictly decreasing from 1 to 0; hence the bound has no interior minimum. At h≤π/2−1 the axial endpoint is sharp; for h≥π/2−1 the horizontal disk is sharp; the triangle inequality is strictly unequal for every genuinely oblique clipped section. Direct Taylor expansions from the independently derived w=cot²θ integral establish the h=1 local threshold and the −Rw²/3 critical quartic term. The exact missing-arc minus chord integral yields the positive 3/2 contact coefficient and C¹/non-C² behavior. The attached standalone checker replayed 1344 numerical diagnostics, including independent polygonal arclengths; infinite claims follow from the analytic proof, not sampled calculations.

value.rationale: Minimizing the Euclidean perimeter of a centered plane section is a natural shape functional for the classical finite circular cylinder, not an ad hoc numerical slice. The global transition at H=(π−2)R is separate from a local stability transition at H=2R, producing a meaningful metastable interval and a complete exact equality classification. The sharp 3/2 boundary-contact singularity explains the geometric change from elliptical to cap-clipped sections. This is substantive structural understanding without claiming a general theorem for all convex bodies.
